input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-based PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning for Gen AI Studio playgrounds

## Description

Selected only if the provisioning-approach decision confirms the RHOAI-controlled operator layer
delivered by the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) will be available for the
target release: implements PostgreSQL/pgvector lifecycle management in that operator layer,
following the model-registry operator's PostgreSQL auto-provisioning pattern, so that Gen AI Studio
playgrounds with RAG get an auto-provisioned pgvector-backed PostgreSQL instance with no manual
user setup. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry this RHOAI-specific provisioning
logic, which is why the work belongs in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer.

## Scope

- Implement reconciliation of a per-namespace pgvector PostgreSQL instance for Gen AI Studio
  playgrounds in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer: Deployment, Service, Secret, and persistent
  storage, created and owned via the operator's reconciliation loop.
- Use the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`)
  — no custom image build and no Konflux onboarding; the model-registry operator already uses this
  image as its auto-provisioned database image.
- Follow the model-registry operator's PostgreSQL provisioning pattern for resource
  requests/limits, credential handling, and child-resource ownership (garbage collection on
  deletion).
- Scope instances per namespace (per-namespace isolation is the preferred multi-tenant model;
  confirm against the decision record's scoping outcome).
- Expose the provisioned connection details (secret/connection string) so the gen-ai
  backend-for-frontend can consume them when creating playground OGX instances.
- Verify disconnected-install coverage for the PostgreSQL image (the rhods-operator CSV
  RELATED_IMAGE entry claimed by the strategy could not be corroborated against the architecture
  context and must be confirmed during implementation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Gen AI Studio playground with RAG enabled in a namespace results in an auto-provisioned
  PostgreSQL instance with pgvector available, with no manual user setup steps.
- Instances are isolated per namespace (multi-tenant scoping per the decision record).
- Resource requests/limits start from the model-registry operator's PostgreSQL sizing, adjusted per
  the pgvector benchmark findings if needed.
- The operator reconciliation loop manages the full instance lifecycle: creation with the
  playground, deletion cleanup, and recovery from drift.
- Provisioning uses the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector; no custom image is built.
- The provisioned connection details are available as a consumable secret/connection reference for
  the playground OGX instance configuration.
- Disconnected-install coverage for the PostgreSQL image is verified and the outcome recorded:
  either the rhods-operator CSV `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` entry (or equivalent
  disconnected-install mirroring configuration) is confirmed to cover
  `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`, or the gap is documented and raised against the
  strategy before release.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning)** — delivered by
  this epic together with the BFF wiring that consumes it.
- **AC-4 (separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance)** — the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance
  is an external process managed by the operator, not an inline provider.
- **AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation)** — per-namespace instance scoping.
- **AC-6 (lightweight for resource-constrained environments)** — sizing derived from the
  model-registry operator's PostgreSQL references and the benchmark findings.

# Wire Gen AI Studio playground OGX instances to the operator-provisioned pgvector vector store

## Description

Selected only if the operator-based provisioning path is chosen: extends the Gen AI Studio gen-ai
backend-for-frontend (in the odh-dashboard repository) so that playground OGXServer instances
created for RAG-enabled playgrounds are configured with the remote pgvector vector_io provider
pointing at the operator-provisioned PostgreSQL instance. The OGX application storage backend stays
on its existing SQLite default — only the vector_io provider configuration changes. The existing
remote vector store implementation in OGX is largely reusable; the integration work is
configuration wiring, not provider development.

## Scope

- Extend the gen-ai BFF's OGXServer instance creation (where OGX storage is currently configured,
  in the Go BFF code that builds the OGXServer spec for the playground) to enable the remote
  pgvector vector_io provider (`ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) and consume the operator-provisioned connection
  details for it.
- Keep OGX application storage on its existing SQLite default; do not consolidate vector and
  application storage in a single database and do not introduce any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL
  application-storage migration path.
- Provide a configuration-level rollback path: because this wiring replaces the vector storage
  previously served by the inline provider being removed from the OGX distribution
  (RHAISTRAT-7474), the pgvector vector_io configuration must be revertible to the prior
  configuration without code changes if a regression is found.
- Document that the default store is positioned for development experimentation: users with
  production-scale vector workloads are directed to an external vector database (no migration-path
  feature is built in this epic).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating a RAG-enabled playground results in an OGX instance whose vector_io provider is remote
  pgvector backed by the operator-provisioned PostgreSQL instance, with no manual user
  configuration.
- Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows (document upload, ingestion, retrieval-augmented chat)
  function against the wired instance with no loss of current capability.
- OGX application storage remains on the SQLite default; only the vector_io provider configuration
  changes.
- The pgvector vector_io configuration can be reverted to the prior configuration without code
  changes (configuration-level rollback), preserving a safety margin before inline providers are
  removed from the OGX distribution.
- All changes pass the odh-dashboard repository's existing build and CI pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning)** — completes the
  out-of-the-box path by consuming the operator-provisioned instance automatically.
- **AC-2 (Playground RAG workflows function, no loss of capability)** — the wiring epic carries the
  end-to-end workflow AC on the same configuration surface it edits.
- **AC-4 (separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance)** — retrieval goes to the external
  PostgreSQL process via the remote provider.
- **AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping)** — connection is scoped to the namespace-isolated instance.

# BFF-managed PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning for Gen AI Studio playgrounds

## Description

Selected only if the provisioning-approach decision rules out the operator-based path for the
release (the RHOAI-controlled operator layer from the dashboard operator modularization,
RHAISTRAT-7164, not landing in time): the Gen AI Studio gen-ai backend-for-frontend provisions the
PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly — similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails
infrastructure — creating the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground
with RAG is configured and no suitable instance exists in the namespace, and wiring the playground
OGX instance's vector_io provider to it.

## Scope

- Implement BFF-managed provisioning: when a playground with RAG is configured and no suitable
  PostgreSQL instance exists in the namespace, the gen-ai BFF creates the PostgreSQL Deployment,
  Service, PVC, and Secret using the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector
  (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`; no custom image build, no Konflux onboarding).
- Configure the playground OGXServer instance's remote pgvector vector_io provider
  (`ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) to consume the provisioned instance; keep OGX application storage on its
  SQLite default (vector storage and application storage are independent configurations — no
  migration path is built).
- Design for portability: when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC becomes
  available (RHOAI 3.6), the BFF must be able to consume the shared connection string rather than
  self-provisioning, without a rewrite of this feature.
- Address lifecycle management explicitly — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop:
  cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts (no orphaned or duplicate instances),
  and credential rotation need explicit design and tests.
- Scope instances per namespace (per-namespace isolation is the preferred multi-tenant model;
  confirm against the decision record's scoping outcome).
- Provide a configuration-level rollback path: the pgvector vector_io configuration must be
  revertible to the prior configuration without code changes if a regression is found, preserving a
  safety margin before inline providers are removed from the OGX distribution.
- Document that the default store is positioned for development experimentation; users with
  production-scale vector workloads are directed to an external vector database.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configuring a playground with RAG results in a namespace-scoped PostgreSQL/pgvector instance and
  an OGX instance using it via the remote pgvector vector_io provider, with no manual user setup
  steps.
- Deleting the playground cleans up the provisioned PostgreSQL resources (Deployment, Service, PVC,
  Secret).
- Restarting the BFF neither orphans nor duplicates the provisioned instance; lifecycle behavior
  for pod restarts and credential rotation is implemented and tested.
- The provisioning code path is structured so a shared platform connection string can be consumed
  instead of self-provisioning without a rewrite (portability to the RHOAI 3.6 platform-provided
  database).
- OGX application storage remains on the SQLite default; only the vector_io provider configuration
  changes.
- The pgvector vector_io configuration can be reverted to the prior configuration without code
  changes (configuration-level rollback).
- Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows function against the provisioned instance with no loss of
  current capability, and all changes pass the odh-dashboard repository's existing build and CI
  pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning)** — delivered by
  BFF self-provisioning.
- **AC-2 (Playground RAG workflows function, no loss of capability)** — provisioning and wiring are
  bundled here because they edit the same BFF code paths and configuration surface; splitting would
  double-touch the same call sites.
- **AC-4 (separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance)** — the PostgreSQL instance is an
  external process in the namespace, not an inline provider.
- **AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation)** — namespace-scoped provisioning.
- **AC-6 (lightweight for resource-constrained environments)** — sizing starts from the
  model-registry operator's PostgreSQL references, adjusted per the pgvector benchmark findings.

# Bring-your-own PostgreSQL configuration path for Gen AI Studio RAG

## Description

Selected only if the provisioning-approach decision rules out both self-provisioning paths for the
release: the degraded fallback in which customers bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities
in the Playground. Users manually configure the OGXServer custom resource spec with their
PostgreSQL/pgvector connection details. This path does not satisfy the out-of-the-box experience
the strategy asks for — it is a release fallback that aligns with the breaking changes introduced
in OGX 1.0, and its limitations must be explicit.

## Scope

- Validate the OGXServer custom resource configuration path for a user-supplied
  PostgreSQL/pgvector connection: connection details supplied via secret, consumed by the OGX
  instance's remote pgvector vector_io provider (`ENABLE_PGVECTOR`).
- Verify that OGX application storage is unaffected (remains on its SQLite default) when only the
  vector_io provider is pointed at the user-supplied database — no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL
  application-storage migration is involved.
- Document the supported setup steps: creating the connection secret, the OGXServer spec fields
  involved, enabling the pgvector vector_io provider, and the scope limitations (development
  experimentation; production-scale vector workloads belong on an external vector database).
- Document explicitly that this path requires manual provisioning and therefore does not meet the
  strategy's out-of-the-box acceptance criterion; the gap is a known consequence of the fallback
  decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validated configuration path exists for using an external, user-provided PostgreSQL/pgvector
  instance with a playground OGX instance (OGXServer spec with user-supplied connection details
  via secret).
- Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows function against the user-provided store via the remote
  pgvector vector_io provider with no loss of current capability for users who complete the setup.
- Setup documentation exists covering secret creation, the OGXServer spec fields, enabling the
  pgvector vector_io provider, and reverting the configuration; the documentation is technically
  reviewed against the validated configuration.
- OGX application storage remains on the SQLite default; only the vector_io provider configuration
  changes.
- The manual-setup limitation versus the out-of-the-box experience is documented and communicated
  as a release note item.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-2 (Playground RAG workflows function, no loss of capability)** — satisfied for users who
  provision and configure their own store.
- **AC-4 (separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance)** — the store is an external
  user-provided PostgreSQL process.
- **AC-1 (out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning)** — **not satisfied by this branch**; this is the
  documented degraded fallback (see the decomposition summary's health warnings). Recorded here so
  reviewers see the gap is analyzed rather than missed.

# Decide the provisioning approach for the Gen AI Studio default pgvector vector store

## Description

This investigation resolves the one genuine unknown that gates all provisioning implementation for
the default vector store strategy: which of three bounded paths Gen AI Studio uses to make a
PostgreSQL/pgvector instance available to playground RAG workflows in the target RHOAI release —
operator-based provisioning in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer delivered by the dashboard
operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164), BFF-managed self-provisioning by the gen-ai
backend-for-frontend, or a bring-your-own PostgreSQL configuration path for users. It also confirms
the scoping model for the default store (per-namespace vs per-instance isolation). The Staff
Engineer Input directs the development team to define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of
sprint planning; this investigation produces that decision.

## Scope

- Track the delivery status of RHAISTRAT-7164 (dashboard operator modularization) against the
  RHOAI 3.5 timeline. It is a hard dependency for the operator-based path: until it delivers, there
  is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. The upstream
  ogx-k8s-operator cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic.
- Define the go/no-go criteria for the release decision: the latest date at which each path remains
  viable for the release, and the evidence each path needs (operator layer availability, BFF
  provisioning design feasibility, acceptance of a degraded bring-your-own experience).
- Evaluate the three provisioning paths against: lifecycle management (cleanup on playground
  deletion, pod-restart handling, credential rotation — the BFF is not an operator with a
  reconciliation loop), multi-tenant isolation, and portability to the platform-provided shared
  PostgreSQL managed via the DSC that is planned for RHOAI 3.6 (for 3.5, Gen AI Studio must
  provision its own PostgreSQL instance).
- Confirm the scoping model for the default vector store. Per-namespace isolation is the preferred
  model; the per-instance motivation came from Auto Rag, which is out of scope for this strategy
  (Auto Rag compatibility is addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824 for RHOAI 3.6).
- Produce a decision record that names the selected provisioning path, the go/no-go criteria, the
  evidence used, and the confirmed scoping model, and hand it to sprint planning for scheduling of
  the corresponding implementation work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written decision record exists that names the selected provisioning path (operator-based,
  BFF-managed, or bring-your-own PostgreSQL) together with the go/no-go criteria and the evidence
  used to select it.
- The record states the assessed delivery status of RHAISTRAT-7164 and the date or trigger after
  which each fallback path applies for the release.
- The scoping model (per-namespace or per-instance isolation) for the default vector store is
  confirmed and recorded in the decision record.
- The decision, including its implications for the out-of-the-box experience if the
  bring-your-own fallback is selected, is presented at sprint planning and the outcome is recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, e.g. per-namespace isolation)** — the scoping model is decided here
  and inherited by the provisioning implementations.
- **AC-1 (out-of-the-box default vector store)** — this decision determines which provisioning
  implementation can satisfy the no-manual-setup requirement for the release.
- **AC-4 (separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance)** — the decision record confirms every
  candidate path provisions an external PostgreSQL process rather than an inline provider.

# Benchmark pgvector and validate Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows

## Description

This epic delivers the sprint-1 risk-reduction validation for choosing pgvector as the default
vector store for Gen AI Studio: a benchmark comparing pgvector against the inline Milvus baseline,
and an end-to-end validation of Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows against an OGX instance
configured with the remote pgvector vector_io provider. Per the Staff Engineer Input, the default
pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation — strict latency SLAs are not required;
the benchmark verifies pgvector is in the same order of magnitude as the inline Milvus baseline,
not that it meets a specific threshold. This validation is scoped to Gen AI Studio Playground RAG
workflows only; Auto Rag compatibility is out of scope (RHAISTRAT-7824).

## Scope

- Stand up a PostgreSQL instance with pgvector using the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image
  (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` includes pgvector out of the box; no custom image build
  and no Konflux onboarding are needed). A manually provisioned test instance is sufficient — this
  epic does not depend on any product provisioning path.
- Configure an OGX server instance with the remote pgvector vector_io provider (enabled via the
  `ENABLE_PGVECTOR` provider configuration), leaving OGX application storage on its existing SQLite
  default. Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations; there is no
  SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because application storage is not being touched.
- Exercise Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows end to end (document upload, ingestion,
  retrieval-augmented chat) over representative small document sets.
- Capture the inline Milvus baseline metrics for the same operations and measure pgvector against
  it. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets, so flat scan (no vector index) is
  the expected operating mode.
- Record recommended PostgreSQL resource requests/limits, starting from the model-registry
  operator's PostgreSQL sizing as the reference point.
- Validate that the OGX distribution functions unchanged with the remote pgvector provider enabled:
  the existing remote vector store implementation is largely reusable, and no OGX distribution code
  changes are expected (passive validation of the distribution).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A benchmark report exists that captures inline Milvus baseline metrics and pgvector metrics for
  the same representative Playground RAG operations (ingestion and retrieval over small document
  sets).
- Measured pgvector performance is within the same order of magnitude as the inline Milvus baseline
  for those operations.
- Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows (document upload, ingestion, retrieval-augmented chat)
  complete successfully against the pgvector-backed OGX instance with no loss of current capability.
- Flat scan (no vector index) is confirmed sufficient for typical Playground document-set sizes, or
  the specific size threshold at which an index becomes necessary is documented.
- Recommended PostgreSQL resource requests/limits are recorded, with the model-registry operator's
  PostgreSQL sizing as the stated starting point.
- OGX application storage remains on its SQLite default throughout the validation; no
  application-storage migration is performed or required.
- The OGX distribution requires no code changes to serve the remote pgvector vector_io provider, or
  any changes found are documented and fed back into the strategy.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-2 (Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store, no loss of
  current capability)** — validated end to end here.
- **AC-4 (default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX instance)** —
  validated: retrieval goes through the remote pgvector provider against an external PostgreSQL
  process, not an inline provider.
- **AC-6 (lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments)** — the benchmark and the
  recorded sizing recommendation are the evidence.
